models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: NAV Rs 115.97 × (long-run ROE − growth) ÷ (cost of equity − growth): ROE 14% / 18% / 22%, growth 5% / 6% / 7%, cost of equity 19.7% / 18.2% / 16.7% (0.61x / 0.98x / 1.55x book).

models.name: P/E on normal earnings
models.comment: Normal 2026/27 EPS of Rs 20 / 23 / 26 at 3.5x / 4.5x / 5.5x, below the justified 4.4x / 5.5x / 7.0x. The base EPS is 21% below the Rs 29.28 twelve-month run-rate on purpose: that figure includes about Rs 4bn of provisions released in the second half of 2025/26, and provisions are now being charged again.

models.name: Dividend model
models.comment: Rs 7 / 8 / 10 next year, growing 5% / 8% / 10% (within the supported 9–15%) for five years; then EPS grows at 5% / 6% / 7% with the stable payout 1 − g ÷ ROE (64% / 67% / 68%), at the cost of equity. Higher than the 13 Nov hand-worked Rs 76 mainly because the published two-stage formula lets the payout rise from a third to about two-thirds once growth slows.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: Used instead of a cash-flow DCF: book Rs 115.97 plus profit above the 18.2% required return; ROE moves from about 21% now to 14% / 18% / 22% over five years, 35% payout, then excess returns grow at 5% / 6% / 7%.

modelsNote: Four equity methods, all computed by scripts/valuation.py from modelInputs; no cash-flow DCF for a finance company. Growth check: the calculator gives 24.2% supported growth (80% kept × 30.1% ROE) because the cash paid in 2025/26 was the previous year's Rs 6; on the Rs 10 declared (67% kept) × the 18% base ROE it is about 12%. The 5% / 8% / 10% dividend growth and 5–7% long-run growth are below it in every case. Ratio check (docs/ratio-ranges.md): beta 0.97 and cost of equity 18.2% are in range; long-run growth is below the 12.24% bond yield; chosen P/Es are below the justified P/E. Base EPS is 21% below the run-rate, for the provision-release reason given under P/E.

scenarios.common: Cost of equity from the house formula: risk-free 8.24% (12.24% bond less a 4.0% default spread) + beta 0.97 × (4.2% + 6.08% country premium). Starting NAV Rs 115.97 (30 Sep 2026); 318.1m shares. H1 EPS is Rs 11.92, so base 2026/27 EPS of Rs 23 needs the second half slightly below the first-half pace.

sensitivity.title: Residual income base case, Rs per share
sensitivity.note: Rs 96.20 is what an 18.2% cost of equity gives if long-run ROE settles at about 15.7%, near the 2019/20–2023/24 level.

fullText:
Summary: Commercial Credit and Finance (COCR.N0000) is a Kandy-based leasing, gold-loan and finance company controlled by the Egodage family's B G Investments (about 50%). At Rs 96.20 it trades at 0.83x NAV of Rs 115.97 and 3.3x trailing earnings, pays Rs 10 a share (a 10.4% yield), and sits about 13% below my fair value of Rs 111. The catch is that 2025/26 profit of Rs 9.75bn (EPS Rs 30.66, ROE 30%) was boosted by a Rs 4.96bn release of old loan-loss provisions as gross bad loans fell from 26% to 4.7%. The September 2026 half-year shows a more normal level: profit down 10% to Rs 3.79bn (EPS Rs 11.92, about 21% ROE), with provisions charged again (Rs 846mn) and interest costs up 34%. I value it on normal EPS of about Rs 23 for 2026/27, not the Rs 29 of the last twelve months. Using the site's standard required return (18.2%, from a 0.97 finance-sector beta), four equity methods put fair value at Rs 111. I'd buy at Rs 94.50 or lower, just under today's price, and treat Rs 83.35 as a strong buy. The business passes three of four tests (high returns, very strong capital, cash dividends) but profit isn't steady, so it stays on the watch list. The big shareholder change: Group Lease Holdings (in liquidation) sold its 30% stake between April and September, spread across new holders, lifting the public holding from 29.5% to 49%.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 96.20, CSE close on 25 November 2026. July–September 2026 range Rs 96.50–122.00.
Six months to September 2026 (group, unaudited): profit after tax Rs 3.79bn, down 10%; EPS Rs 11.92 against Rs 13.30. Net interest income up 10% to Rs 11.6bn, interest expense up 34%, provision charge Rs 846mn against a Rs 957mn release, other costs up 37%, TVS Lanka associate Rs 705mn.
2025/26 (group, audited): profit Rs 9.75bn (up 59%), EPS Rs 30.66, ROE 30.1%, NAV Rs 114.04. Provision release Rs 4.96bn. Gross NPL 4.71% (26.07%), core capital 27.02%. Dividend Rs 10 (Rs 3 interim + Rs 7 final).
Balance sheet at September 2026: leases and loans Rs 95.6bn (down 3.4%), deposits Rs 60.4bn (up 9%), bank borrowing Rs 27.2bn, equity Rs 36.9bn, NAV Rs 115.97.

Required return: 8.24% risk-free + beta 0.97 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 18.2% (bear 19.7%, bull 16.7%).

Valuation table (Rs per share)
Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
Justified price to book | 71.0 | 114.1 | 179.3 | 114.2
P/E on normal earnings | 70.0 | 103.5 | 143.0 | 101.4
Dividend model | 68.3 | 107.0 | 170.5 | 108.1
Residual income | 73.8 | 119.2 | 195.6 | 120.9
Average | 70.8 | 111.0 | 172.1 | 111.1

Assumptions (bear / base / bull)
Cost of equity 19.7% / 18.2% / 16.7%; long-run ROE 14% / 18% / 22%; growth 5% / 6% / 7%; 2026/27 EPS 20 × 3.5 / 23 × 4.5 / 26 × 5.5; next dividend Rs 7 / 8 / 10 growing 5% / 8% / 10% for five years, then the stable payout 1 − g ÷ ROE. Base EPS is 21% below the Rs 29.28 run-rate because that includes about Rs 4bn of provisions released in the second half of 2025/26.
Growth check: supported growth about 12% (67% of profit kept on the Rs 10 dividend × 18% ROE; 24.2% on the calculator's cash-paid basis); every scenario is below it.

Business tests: 3 of 4 passed (fails steady profit); a good business priced between fair value and the buy price: watch list (category unchanged).

Management: no growth or profit targets; plans are better credit quality, a deposit-led funding mix, EV leasing and capital from retained profit. Funding and capital promises are on track; asset quality is too early to judge, with provisions back.

Shareholders: B G Investments (Egodage family) 50.26%. Group Lease Holdings (in liquidation) sold its 29.99% between April and September 2026; public holding 49.00% (29.51% in March).

500-share plan
150 shares up to Rs 96.20, 200 up to Rs 94.46, 150 up to Rs 83.35: about Rs 45,800 in total.

Uncertain: the annual report gives a 2025/26 price range of Rs 103–140, which doesn't match the Rs 89.40 low the September 2025 interim gave for July–September 2025. No September 2026 NPL or capital ratios in the interim. No local 5-year beta could be found, so the sector beta is used. Earlier year-end prices (for P/E history before 2024/25) weren't in the reports read.

No local 5-year betas found (Simply Wall St 1.14 with no window stated; TradingView 1.51 is a 1-year beta). Refresh in January 2027.
